hints: Notice the word always in every statement, so one counterexample is enough to eliminate an option.
Recall that combustion gives out heat, while making a compound from its elements can either give out or take in heat.
Think about the core ionic equation $H^+(aq) + OH^-(aq) \rightarrow H_2O(l)$, where a new bond is made, so decide what sign the enthalpy must always have.
walkthrough:
**Remember what the sign tells us**

Negative $\Delta H$ means exothermic, heat is released. Positive $\Delta H$ means endothermic, heat is absorbed.

Sign rule:
$$\text{exothermic: } \Delta H < 0, \quad \text{endothermic: } \Delta H > 0$$

**Check reaction, combustion and formation**

Reactions in general can be exothermic or endothermic, so they are not always negative. Combustion is burning in oxygen and always releases heat, so it is always negative, not positive.

$$\text{combustion example: } CH_4 + 2O_2 \rightarrow CO_2 + 2H_2O \quad \Delta H < 0$$

**Spot why neutralisation is special**

Formation from elements can be exothermic or endothermic, so it is not always positive. Neutralisation always includes the same step of making water, which releases energy.

Core equation:
$$H^+(aq) + OH^-(aq) \rightarrow H_2O(l) \quad \Delta H \approx -57 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

**Make the conclusion**

Only the statement about neutralisation is true in every case. It is always exothermic and always negative.

options.A: Incorrect. Enthalpy change of reaction, $\Delta H_r$, can be negative (exothermic) or positive (endothermic). For example, cracking alkanes and thermal decomposition are endothermic.
options.B: Incorrect. Combustion is burning in oxygen and always releases heat to the surroundings. Enthalpy changes of combustion are therefore always negative (exothermic), not positive.
options.C: Incorrect. Enthalpy change of formation can be negative or positive. Many formations are exothermic, but some, such as $NO(g)$ from $N_2$ and $O_2$, are endothermic.
options.D: Correct. Neutralisation of a dilute strong acid by a dilute strong base always involves $H^+(aq) + OH^-(aq) \rightarrow H_2O(l)$. Forming the $O-H$ bond releases energy, so $\Delta H_{neut}$ is always negative, about $-57 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
